No subscription, no pressure. 5/5 from 40 Google reviews Hermetschloostrasse 73, 8048 Zurich Altstetten 2 minutes on foot from the Tram 2 and Bus 31 stops. Open in Google Maps Common Questions Do I need a partner? No, you do not need a partner! Most of our students join solo. We rotate partners during class, which is the best way to learn quickly and meet people in our Zurich community. Do I have to dance a specific role? Will there be enough partners? You choose the role you want to learn — leading or following, regardless of gender . We rotate partners during class and keep the balance of leaders and followers in mind when confirming sign-ups, so you will always have someone to dance with, even if you come alone. Are classes taught in English? Yes, AXcent Dance is an English-speaking dance school in Zurich . Our international teachers lead all classes in English, making it perfect for expats and locals alike. Is it too late to start dancing as an adult? It is never too late! Our Adult Beginner Classes are specifically designed for those who think they have "two left feet." We break everything down step-by-step in a relaxed, fun environment. Can I join a class anytime? Yes! Our classes run continuously, so you can join our drop-in dance classes in Zurich anytime. No need to wait for a new semester to start—just book a free trial . What happens after the free trial? If you enjoyed the class, you simply continue with the course. Courses run in 8-week blocks , and one course per week costs 220 CHF (185 CHF for students). Your first course sign-up comes with 15% off . You can compare all options on our registration page . What happens in my first class? Arrive about ten minutes early so we can welcome you. Every class starts with a short warm-up, then we break the basic step down together, and you rotate partners throughout. By the end of your first hour you will dance a full basic to music. Curious for more? Read our beginner guide . What should I wear? Comfortable clothes you can move in and clean shoes with a smooth sole are perfect. No dance shoes are required for your first class. For more detail, see our guide on what to wear for Bachata . Where exactly is the studio, and how do I get there? We are located at Hermetschloostrasse 73, 8048 Zurich Altstetten , just two minutes on foot from the Tram 2 and Bus 31 stops. You can open the studio in Google Maps or find directions on our contact page . Still deciding? The first class is free. If you are looking for high quality Bachata classes in Zurich, then look no further." Frequently Asked Questions Do I need to start at the beginning of the month? No! Our classes run continuously, so you can join anytime if you have previous experience. New beginners are encouraged to start at the beginning of a cycle or book a private intro session. What if I do not have a partner? No problem at all! We rotate partners during class, so everyone dances with everyone. It is the best way to learn! If you prefer to stay with your own partner, just let the teacher know. How do I know my level? Check our Beginner Guide or ask our instructors during a trial class. We are happy to assess your level and recommend the best class for you. What if I miss a class? We know plans can change, so flexibility is built into your pass. Add any known absences when you register. If an unexpected one-day absence comes up later, let us know before 12:00 on the day you will miss. This gives you breathing room while helping us keep your learning rhythm and class planning consistent. Do we need to rotate partners if we come as a couple? While we usually encourage partner rotation because it helps everyone learn faster, it is completely optional! If you prefer to stay with your partner for the whole class, you are more than welcome to do so. It is your date night, after all. COMPLETE REGISTRATION Frequently Asked Questions What payment methods do you accept? + We accept Twint , Cash , and Bank Transfer . Payment details will be sent to you via email or WhatsApp after you complete your registration. What if I miss a class? Can I catch up? + No worries! Life happens. If you wake up sick, you can declare a sick day in the Student Portal before 12:00 on the same day and we will extend your pass by one class day. For longer breaks — such as holidays or an injury — you can request a pass freeze in the portal and we will adjust your pass dates. Please let us know in advance so we can plan. Is the registration binding? + Yes, registration secures your spot in the course, which is often limited to ensure quality. This helps us to maintain balanced classes with an equal number of leaders and followers. Please review our General Terms and Conditions regarding cancellations. Do you offer trial classes? + Yes! For our beginner courses, we often offer free trial classes before the cycle starts. You can also book a specific trial session via the form on our Home Page . Do we need to rotate partners if we come as a couple? + While we usually encourage partner rotation because it helps everyone learn faster, it is completely optional! If you prefer to stay with your partner for the whole class, you are more than welcome to do so. It's your date night, after all. # Page: Meet the Team | AXcent Dance Team & Philosophy Zurich (about.html)
Description: Meet the AXcent Dance teachers in Zurich. Learn about our philosophy, our instructors, and our passion for Latin dance.

Meet the Team | AXcent Dance Team & Philosophy Zurich AXcent DANCE Home About us Our classes Prices & Registration Events Contact Login More ▾ Room Rental Corporate Events Wedding Dance Private Lessons Gallery Education Beginner Guide Blog FAQ Dance Etiquette Contact Book Free Trial EN | DE AXcent Team Meet the Minds Behind AXcent Dance in Zurich Passion, Technique, and Community. Ale y Xidan We are Ale and Xidan, the founders of AXcent Dance. Our journey began with a shared passion for Bachata Sensual and a vision to create a dance school that goes beyond just teaching steps. We believe in building a community where everyone feels welcome, supported, and inspired to express themselves. As International Artists We have shared our passion in over 12 countries. We are also proud to serve as official judges for the Swiss Championship IDO and are active event organizers, dedicated to elevating the dance community. Our Philosophy Our teaching methodology is built on a strong foundation of technique, musicality, and connection. We do not just teach you what to do, but how to do it with style and fluidity. We draw inspiration from various dance styles to create a unique and modern approach to Bachata. Taught around the world Our Mission We are honored to have been invited to teach and share our passion with dance communities across the globe. 25+ Cities 12 Countries 400+ International Dancers Reached Want to see where we will teach next internationally? Go to Events → CONNECTING THE COMMUNITY Curating World-Class Experiences Beyond the studio, we strive to create exceptional dance experiences. From curating Zurich's largest Dominican event to co-organizing one of Italy's most prestigious congresses, we bring the community together with passion. DOMINICAN BACHATA INTENSIVE BOOTCAMP Zurich's Premier Dominican Event We host the biggest Dominican event in Zurich , creating a home for authentic culture and music in the heart of Switzerland. INTERNATIONAL CONGRESS Milano Sensual Congress Co-organizers of one of Italy's top Bachata Sensual congresses. Top World Artists • 4.5 Star Luxury Hotel Visit the studio Hermetschloostrasse 73, 8048 Zurich Altstetten 2 minutes from Tram 2 and Bus 31 · Open in Google Maps Come meet us in person. The first class is free. # Page: How to Start Bachata in Zurich — A Complete Beginner Guide | AXcent Dance (beginner-guide.html)
Description: Never danced before? This beginner guide covers what to wear, shoes, etiquette, and everything for your first Bachata class in Zurich. No partner needed.

How to Start Bachata in Zurich — A Complete Beginner Guide | AXcent Dance AXcent DANCE Home About us Our classes Prices & Registration Events Contact Login More ▾ Room Rental Corporate Events Wedding Dance Private Lessons Gallery Education Beginner Guide Blog FAQ Dance Etiquette Contact Book Free Trial EN | DE Beginner Resources Your First Bachata Class Starting a new hobby can be exciting. Here is everything you need to know to feel confident, meet new people, and enjoy getting fit on the dance floor. No partner needed No experience required Classes taught in English What to Expect Dance Shoes Roles Etiquette What to Expect Walking into a dance studio for the first time can be intimidating, but finding a new passion should not be. Dancing is a fantastic way to stay active and connect with people outside your usual circle. When you feel ready, check the weekly Bachata schedule . What to Wear Comfort is key! Wear clothes that allow you to move freely. Gym clothes, leggings, or casual wear like jeans are fine. Avoid anything too restrictive. Read Full Guide → Partner Rotation In our classes, we highly suggest rotating partners . It helps you learn faster and meet new people. If you prefer to stay with your own partner, we respect that choice. Shoe Guide Having the right tools makes a huge difference. Protect your knees and turn smoothly. Pro Choice Dance Sneakers There are brands specialized in sneaker dancing shoes. These are highly recommended for leaders and followers. Ask us for a promo code. Great Start Comfortable Sneakers Perfect for your first class! Any comfortable indoor sneaker works. Not Recommended Street Shoes Dirty soles damage the studio floor. Please always bring a separate pair of clean indoor shoes . Roles Bachata is a conversation between two people. Nowadays, anyone is welcome to choose either role. Leader Guides the dance and suggests moves. They are responsible for navigation and safety. Follower Interprets the signals and adds their own style. Etiquette & Hygiene Dancing is a close-contact activity. Please be mindful of your hygiene. Fresh breath — mints are great. Deodorant and a fresh shirt go a long way. Please keep phones away during class so everyone can stay present and focused. Please no chewing gum for safety and respect for teachers and other attendants. What Beginners Say 5/5 from 40 Google reviews "I started at AXcent Dance as a complete beginner and after just a few weeks I can already social dance. Ale and Xidan are fantastic teachers who make learning fun and clear." Laura M, Google Review "Ale and Xidan bachata classes in Zurich are amazing for beginners. The steps are explained clearly, and the atmosphere is super welcoming." Federico M, Google Review "I started dancing bachata about one year ago and it added so much flavour to my life. The teachers combine high technical skills with a warm and welcoming environment." Giulia P, Google Review That is everything you need for lesson one. The rest happens on the floor. # Page: Guide to Bachata Parties in Zurich: Where to Dance Every Night (blog/bachata-parties-zurich-guide.html)
Description: Discover the best Bachata parties and social dance events in Zurich. From Club Silbando to Burkliplatz, find out where to dance every night of the week.

Guide to Bachata Parties in Zurich: Where to Dance Every Night AXcent DANCE Home About us Our classes Prices & Registration Events Contact Login More ▾ Room Rental Corporate Events Wedding Dance Private Lessons Gallery Education Beginner Guide Blog FAQ Dance Etiquette Contact Book Free Trial EN | DE Events March 2, 2026 The Ultimate Guide to Bachata Parties in Zurich By Ale & Xidan · AXcent Dance · Meet your teachers Zurich is home to one of the most vibrant Bachata communities in Europe. Whether it is a Monday night craving or a weekend fever, there is always a place to connect and dance. For many, the hardest part of starting Bachata is knowing where the party is. At AXcent Dance, we believe that social dancing is the soul of our community. It is where you put your weekly class training into practice and truly find your flow. If you are looking to start your journey, our Bachata classes in Zurich are designed to get you social-ready in no time. Here is your nightly map to the best social dance floors in Zurich. Monday: Dancing by the Lake Every Monday, experience the magic of dancing by the lake at Bürkliplatz Open Dancing . It is completely free and incredibly beginner-friendly. The open-air atmosphere makes it the perfect place to overcome those first-time social dance nerves. Dancing outdoors at Bürkliplatz is a Zurich tradition. There is nothing like a sunset over Lake Zurich accompanied by the rhythms of the Dominican Republic. It is a social ecosystem where everyone is welcome. Mid-Week Energy: Tuesday & Thursday Tuesday nights belong to Mi Bachata at Vior Club , right in the heart of the city. It is often the most crowded weeknight, filled with energy and high-level dancers. While Thursdays are quieter, stay tuned to our community groups for spontaneous studio socials or smaller gatherings. The Weekend: High-Energy Clubs 🔥 Friday Night @ Bananenreiferei A multi-floor experience where the Bachata floor typically opens late into the night. It is a ritual for many dancers who enjoy both Salsa and Bachata under one roof. 💃 Club Silbando Specials Mark your calendars for the 4th Friday (Fiesta Bachata) and the 2nd Saturday (Fiesta Pasion) of every month. These events feature workshops by local teachers followed by intense social dancing on dedicated floors. If you are feeling nervous about your first social, do not worry. Read our Beginner Guide to learn about dance etiquette and what to expect. We often join these parties as a group, so you will always see a familiar face from the AXcent family. Ready for the Social Floor? Improve your skills and confidence before heading to the party. Join our community with a free trial class or register for our weekly Bachata courses . You can also view our current dance schedule here . JOIN THE AXCENT COMMUNITY Keep the rhythm going More stories from the studio, or take the first step yourself — the first class is free. # Page: Bachata Sensual vs Dominican Bachata: Which to Learn First (blog/bachata-sensual-vs-dominican.html)
Description: Bachata Sensual or Dominican Bachata? Compare the music, movement, and vibe of each style to find the right AXcent Zurich class to start with.

Bachata Sensual vs Dominican Bachata: Which to Learn First AXcent DANCE Home About us Our classes Prices & Registration Events Contact Login More ▾ Room Rental Corporate Events Wedding Dance Private Lessons Gallery Education Beginner Guide Blog FAQ Dance Etiquette Contact Book Free Trial EN | DE Education July 13, 2026 Bachata Sensual vs Dominican Bachata: Which One Should You Learn First? By Ale & Xidan · AXcent Dance · Meet your teachers Every new student asks the same question in their first week: is this Bachata Sensual or Dominican Bachata? The honest answer is that both live under the AXcent roof, and they feel like two different dances even though they share a name. Here is what actually separates them, and how to decide which one to start with. Same Name, Two Very Different Dances Dominican Bachata is the original. It grew out of the roots and history of Bachata in the Dominican Republic during the 1960s, and it is still danced today the way it has always been danced across the island: fast, playful, and built around footwork and hip movement rather than posing. Bachata Sensual is much younger. It was developed in the early 2000s in Cadiz, Spain, by Korke and Judith, who layered body waves, isolations, and a slower, more theatrical musicality onto the Bachata foundation. Read our full guide to Bachata Sensual if you want the deeper story of how it became the dominant style at congresses worldwide. Both styles share the same four-count basic step and the same guitar-driven music at their core — that is why they still carry the same name, and why what is Bachata, really is worth reading before you pick a lane. Dominican Bachata vs Bachata Sensual: Side by Side 🇩🇴 Dominican Origins Born in the 1960s Dominican Republic as working-class music, danced the same way in living rooms and street parties for over sixty years. No choreography required — just the rhythm and your partner. ✨ Sensual Origins Developed in 2000s Cadiz, Spain , by Korke and Judith, who built a new vocabulary of isolations and body movement on top of traditional Bachata, aimed at the international congress scene. 🎸 Dominican Music Traditional guitar, bongo, and güira, played fast and bright. The classic Bachata sound the dance was built around, with an unmistakable raw, romantic energy. 🎧 Sensual Music Modern pop and R&B Bachata remixes with atmospheric production, dramatic builds, and pauses that give dancers space to interpret the music slowly and dramatically. ⚡ Dominican Footwork Fast, intricate footwork with playful hip action and quick turn patterns. The energy stays high, and the focus is on rhythm and musicality in the feet. 💕 Sensual Connection Body waves, chest isolations, and a close embrace where movement is shared slowly between partners. This is where Bachata Sensual earns its name. Aitor Gomez, headline instructor of our Dominican Bachata Bootcamp, mid-movement. Which Style Fits Your Personality? There is no wrong answer here, but most people lean one way once they hear the two styles described honestly. Choose Dominican Bachata if... You want to dance Bachata the way it has been danced in the Dominican Republic for generations. You are drawn to fast footwork and high-energy social dancing, and you want a strong foundation before layering anything modern on top. Choose Bachata Sensual if... You are drawn to close connection, body movement, and slow musicality. You want to develop control over waves and isolations, and you want a style that transfers directly to congresses and socials internationally, where Sensual is now the dominant style. You Do Not Have to Choose Just One In practice, most dancers eventually learn both, and neither path is a dead end. Our Bachata Beginner 1 course builds the fundamental step, timing, and lead-and-follow connection that both styles are built on. From there, you can continue toward the fast footwork of the Dominican tradition, or move into our Bachata Sensual Foundation course to start developing body isolations and styling. Cross-training between the two makes you a more complete dancer either way. Dominican Bachata sharpens your rhythm and footwork, while Bachata Sensual sharpens your connection and body control. Check our weekly class schedule to see where each track currently fits. Want to go deep on the Dominican side? Aitor Gomez and Sarah La Morena return to AXcent this October. Want to Try Dominican Bachata at Full Intensity? If the Dominican side of this comparison is calling to you, the fastest way to experience it properly is our Dominican Bachata Bootcamp on October 17 to 19, 2026, with international instructors Aitor Gomez and Sarah La Morena. Read what to expect at the bootcamp before you book your place. Frequently Asked Questions What is the real difference between Bachata Sensual and Dominican Bachata? Dominican Bachata is the traditional style from the Dominican Republic, built around fast footwork, hip movement, and a playful social energy. Bachata Sensual is a modern style developed in Spain in the 2000s, built around body waves, isolations, and a slower, more theatrical connection. Both share the same basic step and the same musical roots. Which style is better for a complete beginner? Neither style requires prior experience, and both start from the same Beginner 1 course at AXcent Dance. Some students find the Dominican footwork more intuitive because it is faster and more rhythm-driven, while others prefer starting with Bachata Sensual because the pace is slower and easier to process while learning connection. Can I learn both Bachata Sensual and Dominican Bachata at the same time? Yes. Many AXcent students train in both tracks in parallel once they have the fundamentals down. Cross-training improves footwork, connection, and musicality faster than focusing on a single style alone. Does AXcent Dance in Zurich teach both styles? Yes. AXcent Dance in Zurich Altstetten runs dedicated Bachata Beginner courses alongside a full Bachata Sensual track, plus periodic intensives such as the Dominican Bachata Bootcamp with international instructors. Check the weekly schedule for current class times. Come Feel the Difference Yourself Reading about it only gets you so far. Book a free trial class at AXcent Dance in Zurich and try the fundamentals both styles share, no partner or experience required. You can always register for a class once you know which track calls to you. # Page: Connection 101: How to Improve Your Social Dancing | AXcent Dance Blog (blog/connection-101.html)
Description: It is not about the moves, it is about the feeling. 3 simple tips to instantly improve your connection with any partner.

Connection 101: How to Improve Your Social Dancing | AXcent Dance Blog AXcent DANCE Home About us Our classes Prices & Registration Events Contact Login More ▾ Room Rental Corporate Events Wedding Dance Private Lessons Gallery Education Beginner Guide Blog FAQ Dance Etiquette Contact Book Free Trial EN | DE Dance Tips • December 7, 2025 Connection 101: How to Improve Your Social Dancing By Ale & Xidan · AXcent Dance · Meet your teachers We have all been there: you learn a complex turn pattern in class, execute it perfectly with the instructor, but when you try it on the social dance floor... it falls apart. Why? Often, it is not the move—it is the connection. In Bachata Sensual , connection is everything. It is the invisible conversation between two bodies. Without it, we are just two people doing math next to each other. With it, we are creating art. Here are three simple ways to instantly improve your connection. 1. The Frame: Firm but Breathable Think of your frame like a steering wheel. It needs to be firm enough to transmit information, but flexible enough to turn safely. A common mistake is "spaghetti arms" (too loose) or "robot arms" (too stiff). Tip: Engage your back muscles, not just your arms. Your arms should feel like extensions of your core. This allows for a specialized tension that is responsive yet stable. 2. Listening vs. Speaking Leading is like speaking, and following is like listening. If the leader is shouting (using too much force), the follower stops listening. If the follower interrupts (anticipates the move), the conversation breaks down. Followers: Wait for the signal. Do not guess. It is better to be a split-second late than early. Leaders: Be clear but gentle. Invite the movement, do not force it. Our dance etiquette guide covers more about leading and following with respect. 3. Eye Contact and Presence You do not need to stare into your partner's soul for the entire song, but acknowledging them is crucial. A smile, brief eye contact, and simply being "present" (not looking around the room for your next partner) changes the entire vibe of the dance. When you focus on the person in front of you, the connection naturally deepens. The best dances are not about the coolest moves; they are about the shared energy in that 3-minute moment. If you are just getting started, our beginner guide will help you feel confident from day one. To start practicing these skills immediately, check our weekly Bachata schedule or visit our registration page to book your spot. Practice Makes Perfect Want to work on your connection in a friendly environment? Browse our Bachata class schedule or register today to join our community! JOIN US Keep the rhythm going More stories from the studio, or take the first step yourself — the first class is free. # Page: Frame Technique in Bachata: Dance Tips Episode 1 | AXcent Dance Blog (blog/dance-tips-1-frame.html)
Description: Improve your Bachata leading and following with better frame technique. Learn the do's and don'ts of arm positioning and connection.

Frame Technique in Bachata: Dance Tips Episode 1 | AXcent Dance Blog AXcent DANCE Home About us Our classes Prices & Registration Events Contact Login More ▾ Room Rental Corporate Events Wedding Dance Private Lessons Gallery Education Beginner Guide Blog FAQ Dance Etiquette Contact Book Free Trial EN | DE Education • Dec 27, 2025 Frame Technique in Bachata By Ale & Xidan · AXcent Dance · Meet your teachers Little things make a big difference. Happy dancing! The Importance of Frame Your "frame" is the structure of your arms and upper body. It is the bridge between you and your partner. A solid, comfortable frame allows for clear communication, making leading and following feel effortless. To understand why this matters so much, read our article on connection in social dancing . How to Create a Good Frame A good frame is active but relaxed. Here are the key points to focus on: Shoulders down and wide to release unnecessary tension. Elbows lifted to create space and alignment. Imagine the forearms gently spiraling outward . Imagine the upper arms gently spiraling inward . When you combine these feelings, your arms connect naturally into your back, so you can lead and follow body movements clearly. New to Bachata? Our beginner guide explains the basics step by step, or you can come practice your frame in our Bachata classes in Zurich . Common Mistakes to Avoid Shoulders raised → Creates tension and stiffness. Elbows down → Weakens the frame and reduces connection to the partner. Why it matters? Tense shoulders and dropped elbows disconnect the arms from the back. This makes it harder to lead and follow, and can break the flow of the dance. If you want personalized feedback on your frame, consider booking a private lesson with our instructors. Ready to practice? Join our classes to master your frame and more! Check our schedule or register now to secure your spot. # Page: Find the 1 in Bachata | Musicality Guide | AXcent Zurich (blog/finding-the-one-bachata-musicality.html)
Description: Learn the secret language of Bachata musicality. Discover how to hear the instruments, find the '1', and transform your social dancing in Zurich.

Find the 1 in Bachata | Musicality Guide | AXcent Zurich AXcent DANCE Home About us Our classes Prices & Registration Events Contact Login More ▾ Room Rental Corporate Events Wedding Dance Private Lessons Gallery Education Beginner Guide Blog FAQ Dance Etiquette Contact Book Free Trial EN | DE Music March 28, 2026 Stop Counting, Start Feeling: How to Find the 1 in Bachata Music By Ale & Xidan · AXcent Dance · Meet your teachers For many beginners, hearing "1, 2, 3, tap" feels like trying to solve a puzzle while someone fast-forwards the track. But here is the secret: you should not be counting numbers in your head. You should be listening to the instruments. Understanding Bachata musicality is the defining difference between doing steps on a dance floor and truly expressing music. At our Bachata classes in Zurich , we emphasize moving away from counting and moving toward feeling. For the full sound foundation, read our guide to Bachata music and dance . Let's break down the secret language of Bachata so you can find the "1" automatically. The Core Instruments of Bachata 🥁 The Bongo The heartbeat of the dance. In the basic step, the bongo provides the deep "martillo" pattern. The sharp hit (the martillo) lands right on the 4 and the 8—the exact moment you tap. 🎶 The Güira The metallic scraping sound driving the rhythm forward. It acts like a metronome, keeping the energy high, especially during the fast-paced "Mambo" sections. 🎸 The Bass Guitar The foundation underneath. The bass emphasizes the "1," the "3," and the "4." Listening for its heavy plunge is one of the easiest ways to center yourself back on the "1." 🎸 The Requinto (Lead Guitar) The emotion. This is the melody that tells the story. While the bongo keeps you on time, the requinto dictates your styling, body movement, and feeling. How to Translate Sound to Movement To truly find the 1, you must let your body respond to the distinct sections of a Bachata song: the Derecho, the Majao, and the Mambo. We cover these essential concepts extensively in our beginner guide . The Derecho: The verses. This is smooth, intimate, and grounded. The bongo is steady. You dance your basic steps smoothly. The Majao: The chorus. The energy lifts. The bongo player switches from striking the skin with hands to hitting it with sticks (or playing the cowbell in modern tracks). Here, your energy should expand. The Mambo: The instrumental section. High energy, sharp hits, fast footwork. This is the peak of the dance. If you ever lose the "1," simply pause. Do not panic. Listen for the strong, low note of the bass, or wait for the singer to begin a new phrase. Music works in 8-count blocks. Take a breath, wait for the next phrase to start, and step boldly on the 1. Mastering this takes practice, which is why we invite you to refine your ear at our upcoming classes . Master the Music Are you ready to stop counting and start dancing? Join our foundation classes to build your confidence and musicality. View our Bachata schedule or register for our courses in Zurich. How to Act on Your Happiness This Zurich Spring | AXcent Dance AXcent DANCE Home About us Our classes Prices & Registration Events Contact Login More ▾ Room Rental Corporate Events Wedding Dance Private Lessons Gallery Education Beginner Guide Blog FAQ Dance Etiquette Contact Book Free Trial EN | DE Wellness April 5, 2026 How to Act on Your Happiness This Zurich Spring: The Science-Backed Way to Bloom By Ale & Xidan · AXcent Dance · Meet your teachers As the Zurich lakeside bursts into blossom and the days stretch longer, there is a palpable sense of renewal in the air. # Page: Swiss Salsa & Bachata Championship | AXcent Judges (blog/ido-swiss-championship-salsa-bachata-judges-2026.html)
Description: AXcent Dance judges Salsa and Bachata at the Open Swiss Championship 2026 in Solothurn, connecting Zurich dancers to IDO standards.

Swiss Salsa & Bachata Championship | AXcent Judges AXcent DANCE Home About us Our classes Prices & Registration Events Contact Login More ▾ Room Rental Corporate Events Wedding Dance Private Lessons Gallery Education Beginner Guide Blog FAQ Dance Etiquette Contact Book Free Trial EN | DE Events • May 5, 2026 AXcent Dance Judges Salsa and Bachata at the Swiss Championship By Ale & Xidan · AXcent Dance · Meet your teachers This weekend, on Saturday, May 9, 2026 , AXcent Dance will represent Zurich at the Open Swiss Championship 2026 in Solothurn as judges for Salsa and Bachata. For our studio, this is more than a calendar note. It is a recognition of the technical standard, musical knowledge, and teaching integrity that we bring into every Bachata class in Zurich. An Official Swiss Dance-Sport Stage The championship is listed in the Swiss IDO tournament system as the Offene Schweizermeisterschaft in Solothurn on 9.5.2026 . The same tournament listing names a broad field of categories, including Salsa, Salsa Solo, Salsa Group, Salsa Formation, Bachata, Bachata Solo, Bachata Group, Bachata Formation, Bachata Jack and Jill, Bachata Dominicana, Bachata Sensual, Bachata Urban, Kizomba, Merengue, Caribbean Show, Rueda, and Synchrodance. The public event page confirms the date, time, and location: May 9, 2026, from 09:30 to 23:55 at Konzertsaal Solothurn. It also describes the event as a varied dance experience with Salsa, Bachata, Kizomba, Merengue, Jack and Jill competitions, group formations, and show categories. You can read the official ticket and event information on Eventfrog . Why IDO Context Matters IDO Switzerland is the Swiss national structure connected to the International Dance Organization. Its own organization page lists specialized Swiss dance bodies, including Swiss Salsa Federation for Salsa, Bachata, Jack and Jill, Merengue, Caribbean Dances, Caribbean Show, and Salsa Rueda de Casino, alongside SFBT, the Schweizerischer Fachverband Breitensport Tanz. This gives the championship a formal national framework rather than a casual social-event context. Internationally, the International Dance Organization describes itself as a non-profit world dance and dancesport federation with more than 90 member and contact nations. Judging at an event connected to that ecosystem means working with standards that reach beyond one local scene. What This Says About AXcent Dance Being invited to judge Salsa and Bachata at the Swiss Championship is a strong signal for our students. It shows that AXcent Dance is not only active in social dancing and weekly classes, but also trusted in a competition environment where timing, technique, musicality, partnering, presentation, and fairness all matter. That matters inside our studio as well. When we teach Bachata, Bachata Sensual, Salsa concepts, musicality, leading, following, and partner connection, we are not teaching isolated moves. We are building dancers with the same attention to quality that is required when evaluating competitors on a Swiss championship floor. Representing Zurich Bachata We are proud to represent our Zurich Bachata community at this event. It is an opportunity to support dancers, honour the work of organizers, and help connect Swiss social dance culture with a broader international dance-sport standard. If you train with us, this is part of what you are connected to: a studio that keeps learning, contributing, and showing up where quality matters. The event also became a proud student win for our studio: AXcent Dance earned IDO Swiss Bachata silver through Alex Elsig in Bachata Jack and Jill Leader 17+. Read the full story about AXcent's Bachata silver at the IDO Swiss Championship . # Page: Unleashing Your Style: Why Lady Styling Is More Than Bachata (blog/lady-styling-zurich-guide.html)
Description: Discover the power of femininity with Bachata Lady Styling in Zurich. Unleash your style through modern and contemporary concepts. Join AXcent Dance today.

Unleashing Your Style: Why Lady Styling Is More Than Bachata AXcent DANCE Home About us Our classes Prices & Registration Events Contact Login More ▾ Room Rental Corporate Events Wedding Dance Private Lessons Gallery Education Beginner Guide Blog FAQ Dance Etiquette Contact Book Free Trial EN | DE Artistry March 21, 2026 Unleashing Your Style: Why Lady Styling Is More Than Bachata By Ale & Xidan · AXcent Dance · Meet your teachers For many, Bachata is a dance of connection with a partner. But there is a hidden dimension to this art form—one that is strictly personal, deeply feminine, and incredibly empowering. It is the world of Lady Styling , and at AXcent Dance, we believe it is the key to truly unleashing your unique identity on the dance floor. Lady Styling is about finding your own voice through movement. It Is Not Just Bachata A common misconception is that Lady Styling in Zurich is simply about adding arm flourishes to your basic step. In reality, it is a holistic dance discipline. Our Lady Styling classes integrate concepts from modern and contemporary dance , focusing on body awareness, isolation, and fluid mechanics. By learning these contemporary concepts, you do not just learn "moves"—you learn how your body functions as an instrument. Whether it is a subtle head roll or a complex contemporary-influenced body wave, the goal is to make every movement look intentional and effortless. ✨ Modern Concepts We use contemporary dance techniques to improve your balance, core strength, and the quality of your movement. 🌊 Body Awareness Learn to isolate every muscle group. Deep body awareness is the foundation of elegant styling and powerful expression. Mastering the art of dance starts with self-expression and solo movement. Unleashing Your Style The most beautiful thing about dance is that no two people move the same way. Lady Styling is the practice of unleashing your unique style . It is a safe space to experiment with different energies—from the sharp and intense to the soft and romantic. In our studio, we encourage followers to break away from being "reactive" and start being "proactive." When you understand the music and your own body, you are no longer just following a lead; you are contributing to a shared piece of art with your own feminine flair. Femininity in Motion Femininity is not a single look—it is an energy. Our classes are designed to help you tap into that energy and express it through modern Bachata concepts . It is about confidence, poise, and the courage to be seen. As you progress, you will notice that this confidence spreads far beyond the studio doors. The posture, the grace, and the self-assuredness you develop in Lady Styling will stay with you in your everyday life in Zurich. If you are new to the scene, check out our Beginner Guide to see how to start your journey. Beyond Gender: Styling in 2026 While the term "Lady Styling" is deeply rooted in dance tradition, the landscape in 2026 has evolved. Today, styling is seen as universal body expression . These classes are no longer exclusive to one gender; they are for any dancer who wishes to master the nuances of body movement. We see an increasing number of leaders joining these sessions to improve their own fluidity and musicality. Whether you identify as a follower or a leader, the concepts of isolations, arm placement, and contemporary flow are essential tools for any modern dancer. It is about styling in general —mastering the art of being yourself on the floor. Ready to Find Your Style? Join our Open Level Lady Styling course every Thursday. Experience a community of supportive women and discover the dancer you were meant to be. View our weekly schedule or register online today . # Page: Roots of Bachata: History, Origins & Prohibition | AXcent (blog/roots-of-bachata.html)
Description: Discover where Bachata was born, why it was prohibited, and its gritty history from Dominican roots to a global phenomenon in Zurich.

Roots of Bachata: History, Origins & Prohibition | AXcent AXcent DANCE Home About us Our classes Prices & Registration Events Contact Login More ▾ Room Rental Corporate Events Wedding Dance Private Lessons Gallery Education Beginner Guide Blog FAQ Dance Etiquette Contact Book Free Trial EN | DE Education / History • Updated July 9, 2026 The Roots of Bachata: Origins, History & Prohibition Chapters The Origins History of Prohibition Essential Instruments The Rise to Global Stage UNESCO World Heritage Bachata Today 7 Surprising Facts By Ale & Xidan · AXcent Dance · Meet your teachers Today, Bachata is danced in sleek studios and massive congresses from Zurich to Tokyo. But if you have ever wondered "where is Bachata from?" or "where was Bachata born?" , the answer takes us back to humble, gritty beginnings. Born in the rural countryside and marginalized neighborhoods of the Dominican Republic, Bachata is a genre that fought for its voice. If you want to experience this energy firsthand, joining Bachata classes in Zurich is the best way to start your dance journey. Where Was Bachata Born? The Origins Bachata was born in the Dominican Republic in the early 1960s, shortly after the fall of the Trujillo dictatorship. Its roots can be traced back to the Cuban Bolero , Son, and Troubadour traditions. Dominican musicians took the slow, romantic rhythm of the Bolero and infused it with their own flair, using instruments like the Requinto (a smaller lead guitar with a metallic sound), bongo, and güira. This unique combination created the authentic Bachata sound we recognize today. To learn more about the genre and how it is danced, visit our complete guide to Bachata . Why Was Bachata Prohibited in the Past? For decades, Bachata was socially prohibited and fiercely stigmatized. It was originally known as música de amargue — music of bitterness . The lyrics spoke of heartbreak, longing, illicit love, and the struggles of everyday rural life. Because of its association with poverty and rural backwardness, the Dominican high society rejected it. It was labeled as "vulgar" and "low-class," predominantly played in bars, brothels, and shantytowns. Mainstream radio stations refused to play it, and it was effectively banned from acceptable social venues. Yet, the people loved it. It was their truth, strummed on a guitar with a rhythm that compelled you to move. Essential Instruments: The Sound of Bachata To truly appreciate the history, you must understand the "Soul" of the music. Unlike Salsa, which relies on a full brass section, Bachata is defined by its guitar-driven sound. The Requinto is the lead guitar that plays the melodic hooks, while the Segunda (rhythm guitar) adds the complex syncopation. The heartbeat is provided by the Bongo , which anchors the rhythm, especially on the 4th beat. The Güira (metal scraper) adds the high-energy texture, and the Bass provides the deep, walking lines that give Bachata its undeniable groove. Bachata Dance History: The Rise to Acceptance Slowly, the stigma began to fade. Artists like Luis Segura began to bring a more polished sound, reaching a wider audience. But the true explosion happened in the 90s and 2000s. Juan Luis Guerra , a classically trained musician, released the album Bachata Rosa in 1990, winning a Grammy and proving the genre's artistic merit to the world. He bridged the gap between the "lower class" roots and the international stage. Then came Aventura . This group of Bronx-born Dominicans, led by Romeo Santos, infused Bachata with R&B, Pop, and Hip Hop. They created a modern sound that resonated with a global youth generation. Suddenly, Bachata was not just for your parents—it was cool, it was sexy, and it was everywhere. UNESCO: A Victory for Dominican Culture In December 2019, Bachata reached its greatest official milestone. It was officially declared an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity by UNESCO . This recognition validated the struggle of the early 1960s artists who were once marginalized and recognized Bachata as a world-class artistic contribution. Bachata Today Today, the Bachata dance origin story continues to evolve. We have Traditional / Dominican Bachata , staying true to the fast footwork and authentic rhythms. We have Bachata Sensual , born in Spain, focusing on body isolations and connection. And we have Bachata Moderna, blending various styles. Experience the Roots in Zurich Ready to start your own dance journey? From the foundations to the latest styles, we have a class for you. Check our weekly schedule or register today to join our community. BOOK A FREE TRIAL 7 Surprising Facts About Bachata History First Recording : The very first Bachata song was "Que Viva el Amargue" by José Manuel Calderón in 1962. The Name : The word "Bachata" originally meant a "party" or "informal social gathering" in the countryside. Stolen Rhythm : For years, Bachata was so stigmatized that artists had to label their records as "Bolero Campesino" (Country Bolero) to get them sold. The Censorship : Until the mid-80s, you would almost never hear a Bachata song on "respectable" national radio in the DR. Grammy Milestone : Juan Luis Guerra's 'Bachata Rosa' (1990) was the first Bachata album to win a Grammy. Traditional vs. Sensual : Traditional Bachata focuses on rhythmic footwork, while the Sensual style (born in Spain) emphasizes body waves and isolations. Global Presence : Zurich is now home to one of the most vibrant Bachata communities in Switzerland! Quick Facts: Bachata History FAQ Where is Bachata from and where was it born? Bachata is from the Dominican Republic. It was born in the early 1960s in rural neighborhoods and shantytowns after the fall of the Trujillo dictatorship. Why was Bachata prohibited and called 'music of bitterness'? Bachata was socially prohibited because it was associated with poverty and rural life. It was labeled 'música de amargue' (music of bitterness) and banned from mainstream radio for decades. What are the authentic roots of Bachata music? The roots of Bachata lie in the Cuban Bolero, Son, and Troubadour traditions. Dominican musicians adapted these with the Requinto guitar, bongo, and güira to create its unique rhythm. Inspired by the Roots? Experience the authentic rhythm and footwork at our upcoming intensive. # Page: Salsa vs Bachata: Key Differences Every Dancer Should Know (blog/salsa-vs-bachata.html)
Description: Salsa vs Bachata — what is the difference? Compare music, rhythm, and dance style. Find out why most dancers learn both for the complete Latin experience.

Salsa vs Bachata: Key Differences Every Dancer Should Know AXcent DANCE Home About us Our classes Prices & Registration Events Contact Login More ▾ Room Rental Corporate Events Wedding Dance Private Lessons Gallery Education Beginner Guide Blog FAQ Dance Etiquette Contact Book Free Trial EN | DE Education February 14, 2026 Salsa vs Bachata : The Differences Every Dancer Should Know By Ale & Xidan · AXcent Dance · Meet your teachers Salsa or Bachata — which one should you learn? It is one of the most common questions people ask when they first discover Latin dance. Both are incredible social dances, but they feel completely different on the floor. Here is a comprehensive breakdown to help you choose — or convince you to learn both. The heart of the difference lies in the music: Salsa's brass and percussion vs Bachata's strings. Where Do Salsa and Bachata Come From? Understanding the origins of Salsa and Bachata helps explain why they feel so different today. Salsa emerged in 1970s New York City , born from a melting pot of Afro-Cuban rhythms (Son, Mambo, Guaracha), Puerto Rican influences, and American jazz. The Fania All-Stars, Celia Cruz, and Hector Lavoe turned it into a global movement. Today, the main Salsa styles are Salsa On1 (LA style) , Salsa On2 (New York Mambo) , and Cuban Salsa (Casino) . Bachata was born in the 1960s Dominican Republic as the music of the rural working class — often dismissed by the elite as "música de amargue" (music of bitterness). Pioneers like José Manuel Calderón and later Juan Luis Guerra brought it mainstream. For a deeper dive into Bachata's extraordinary history, read our article on the roots and origins of Bachata . It evolved into multiple styles: Bachata Dominicana (traditional, fast footwork), Bachata Sensual (body waves, close connection), and Bachata Moderna (a fusion of both). Salsa vs Bachata: Side-by-Side Comparison 🎺 Salsa Music Fast, energetic, and brass-driven . Congas, timbales, and trumpets create a powerful rhythm at 150–250 BPM . The music makes you want to move fast and sharp. 🎸 Bachata Music Slow, romantic, and guitar-driven . Acoustic guitar, bongos, and güira create a smooth rhythm at 120–140 BPM . The music invites you to feel, not rush. ⚡ Salsa Footwork Quick-quick-slow timing with complex turn patterns, shines, and crossbody leads . Requires speed, precision, and strong core stability. 🌊 Bachata Footwork Simple side-to-side four-step pattern with a signature tap on count 4. Focus is on hip movement, body waves, and the connection between partners . 🤸 Salsa Partner Connection Typically danced in open position with frequent switches between open and closed frames. The lead guides through hand pressure and frame. 💕 Bachata Partner Connection Often danced in a close embrace . Body movement, weight shifts, and musicality are shared intimately. Bachata Sensual is known for its deeply connected, fluid style . Different instruments, different energy: Salsa is percussion-driven, Bachata is guitar-driven. Is Bachata More Sensual Than Salsa? Short answer: usually yes . Bachata — especially Bachata Sensual , which was developed by Korke and Judith in Cadiz, Spain — is danced in close embrace with body waves, isolations, and fluid partner connection. The romantic music naturally encourages a more intimate expression. Salsa, on the other hand, is more about energy, speed, and playfulness . It is less about the physical closeness and more about the dynamic interaction — fast turns, dramatic dips, and synchronized shines. However, Cuban Salsa (Casino) can also be danced in close position and has a warm, playful sensuality of its own. The truth is, both dances can be as sensual or as playful as the dancers choose. It depends on the style, the song, and the individual connection. Why Most Dancers Learn Both At almost every Latin dance social event around the world — from Zurich to Miami — the DJ plays both Salsa and Bachata throughout the night. If you only know one, you are sitting out for half the songs. Learning both makes you a complete Latin dancer : Salsa improves your timing — the faster rhythm challenges your musicality Bachata improves your connection — the slow tempo teaches you to feel your partner Cross-training makes you versatile — your Salsa sharpness adds flair to Bachata, and your Bachata smoothness adds quality to Salsa Double the social opportunities — you can dance all night without sitting out At AXcent Dance in Zurich , our curriculum includes elements of Salsa, Merengue, and ChaCha alongside our core Bachata program. We believe this holistic approach creates dancers who are adaptable, musical, and confident on any dance floor. Check our weekly class schedule to find a level that fits you. Frequently Asked Questions What is the main difference between Salsa and Bachata music? Salsa music is energetic and brass-driven, featuring congas, timbales, and trumpets with a fast tempo. Bachata music is guitar-driven and romantic, with bongos and güira providing a slower, more sensual rhythm. Salsa originated in 1970s New York from Afro-Cuban roots, while Bachata developed in the 1960s Dominican Republic. Can you dance both Salsa and Bachata at the same social event? Absolutely. Most Latin dance social events (called "socials") play both Salsa and Bachata music throughout the night. Knowing both dances means you can dance all night without sitting out. Many dance schools, including AXcent Dance in Zurich, teach both styles. Which dance is more sensual, Salsa or Bachata? Bachata is generally considered more sensual and intimate due to its slower tempo, closer partner connection, and emphasis on body movement and hip rolls. However, different styles exist within both dances — Bachata Sensual is the most intimate style, while Cuban Salsa can also be very close and connected. Should I learn Salsa or Bachata first? Starting with Bachata is often recommended for absolute beginners because of its simpler basic steps and slower tempo. Once comfortable, adding Salsa improves your overall musicality and coordination. Many dancers eventually learn both to become complete Latin dancers. Try Both for Free Still not sure? Browse our class schedule or register for a trial class at AXcent Dance in Zurich and experience the difference yourself. No partner needed, no experience required. # Page: Stress Less, Dance More: The Science Behind the 'Dancer's High' | AXcent Dance Blog (blog/science-of-dance-mental-health.html)
Description: Discover the science behind how partner dancing like Bachata lowers cortisol, boosts endorphins, and improves mental health. Escaping burnout has never been this fun.

Stress Less, Dance More: The Science Behind the 'Dancer's High' | AXcent Dance Blog AXcent DANCE Home About us Our classes Prices & Registration Events Contact Login More ▾ Room Rental Corporate Events Wedding Dance Private Lessons Gallery Education Beginner Guide Blog FAQ Dance Etiquette Contact Book Free Trial EN | DE Health & Wellness • Jan 4, 2026 Stress Less, Dance More: The Science Behind the 'Dancer's High' By Ale & Xidan · AXcent Dance · Meet your teachers We live in a world that never stops pinging, buzzing, and demanding our attention. Stress has become the silent soundtrack of modern life, and for many of us, the "cure" is often another chore: hitting the gym, meditating in silence, or trying the latest detox. But what if the antidote to burnout wasn't another task, but a rhythm? What if the most effective way to reset your nervous system was to simply... dance? The Chemistry of Joy: Cortisol vs. Endorphins When you're stressed, your body is flooded with cortisol . In small doses, it helps you focus. Chronic exposure, however, kills your sleep, dampens your mood, and exhausts your body. Dancing—specifically complex, coordinated movement like Bachata —is a potent cortisol killer. But it doesn't just lower the bad stuff; it floods your brain with the good stuff: endorphins . "The 'Dancer's High' isn't just a metaphor. It's a scientifically measurable state where pain perception drops and euphoria rises, similar to the famous 'runner's high'—but with better music." The Power of Connection: Why Partner Dance is Different You can get endorphins from a treadmill, sure. But partner dancing adds a secret weapon: Oxytocin . Often called the "cuddle hormone," oxytocin is released during positive human connection and touch. In Bachata, the connection isn't just physical; it's communicative. Leading and following requires a level of trust and non-verbal listening that deeply nourishes our social brain. If you are curious about how this partner dynamic works, our guide to social dancing breaks it down. In an increasingly isolated digital world, this human contact is literally healing. Mindfulness in Motion Have you ever tried to worry about your taxes while figuring out a complex turn pattern? It's impossible. Dance demands focus . You have to be present in the music, present with your partner, and present in your body. This creates a state of "flow"—a form of active mindfulness. Unlike sitting meditation, which can be difficult for restless minds, dance forces you into the "now" because if you drift off, you miss the beat! Escaping Burnout, One Step at a Time It’s not just about burning calories (though you’ll do plenty of that). It’s about resetting your emotional baseline. Leaving the studio after a class, you don't just feel tired; you feel alive . So next time you feel the weight of the week pressing down, do not just sit there. Put on a song. Find a partner. And dance it out. Your brain will thank you. Check our weekly class schedule to find the perfect session for your midweek reset. Need a Mental Reset? Come find your "Dancer's High" with us. No experience needed, just bring your stress—and leave it on the floor. # Page: What to Wear to Bachata Class: A Beginner's Guide | AXcent Dance Blog (blog/what-to-wear-bachata.html)
Description: Wondering what to wear for your first Bachata class? Here is our complete guide on clothes, shoes, and hygiene to make you feel confident and comfortable.

What to Wear to Bachata Class: A Beginner's Guide | AXcent Dance Blog AXcent DANCE Home About us Our classes Prices & Registration Events Contact Login More ▾ Room Rental Corporate Events Wedding Dance Private Lessons Gallery Education Beginner Guide Blog FAQ Dance Etiquette Contact Book Free Trial EN | DE Dance Tips / Beginner • December 9, 2025 What to Wear to Bachata Class By Ale & Xidan · AXcent Dance · Meet your teachers Walking into a dance studio for the first time is exciting, but let’s be honest—it also brings up a lot of questions. The most common one? "What should I wear?" The good news is that Bachata is a casual, social dance. You do not need a sequined dress or a tuxedo to start learning! If you are preparing for your very first class, our beginner guide covers everything you need to know. Here is our simple guide to help you look good and feel comfortable on the dance floor. 1. Comfort is King (and Queen) The most important rule is to be comfortable. Bachata involves turns, body rolls, and partner work. You want clothes that move with you, not against you. Tops: Wear a t-shirt or tank top that fits well. Avoid anything too baggy that might get caught during turns. Bottoms: Leggings, gym shorts, or stretchy jeans are perfect. Avoid stiff pants or short skirts/dresses unless you wear shorts underneath. Check: Raise your arms above your head. Does your shirt stay in place? Can you step wide without restriction? If yes, you are good to go! 2. The Shoe Question You definitely don't need professional dance heels for your first class! In fact, we recommend starting flat to build your balance. Indoor Only: Please bring a clean pair of shoes to change into. Street grit spoils the dance floor. Socks: Perfectly fine for your first lesson! They help you spin easily. Sneakers: Wear comfortable sneakers, but try to avoid running shoes with super "grippy" rubber soles, as they can make turning difficult on your knees. Smooth soles are best. 3. Hygiene & Etiquette Bachata is a close dance. Being fresh is just as important as being well-dressed! For more on partner respect and social floor behavior, see our dance etiquette guide . Deodorant: Always a must before class. Mints: A piece of gum or a mint is appreciated by every partner. Extra Shirt: If you tend to sweat, bringing a spare t-shirt to change into halfway through is a pro move. 4. What Not To Wear To keep everyone safe and comfortable, try to avoid: Large Jewelry: Long necklaces or big hoop earrings can get caught. Watches/Bracelets: Heavy watches can accidentally scratch your partner. Sleeveless Shirts (Leaders): It is generally preferred for leads to wear sleeves, as your partner's hand will often be on your shoulder/back. Have more questions about what to expect? Browse our frequently asked questions . Ready to Step Out? Now that you are dressed for success, come join us on the dance floor! Check our weekly schedule or register today . BOOK A FREE TRIAL Keep the rhythm going More stories from the studio, or take the first step yourself — the first class is free. # Page: Bachata Education: History, Styles & Musicality | AXcent (education.html)
Description: The ultimate Bachata knowledge hub. Explore history, street styles, musicality instruments, and terminology with AXcent Dance Zurich.

Bachata Education: History, Styles & Musicality | AXcent AXcent DANCE Home About us Our classes Prices & Registration Events Contact Login More ▾ Room Rental Corporate Events Wedding Dance Private Lessons Gallery Education Beginner Guide Blog FAQ Dance Etiquette Contact Book Free Trial EN | DE Knowledge Base Dance Education Understanding the history, music, and language of Bachata. 01 History 02 Styles 03 Musicality 04 Glossary 1 History 2 Styles 3 Musicality 4 Glossary History of Bachata 1960s Amargue roots Bachata originated in the rural neighborhoods of the Dominican Republic in the early 1960s. Initially, it was known as "amargue" (bitterness) music, reflecting themes of heartbreak, loss, and longing. 1990s International breakthrough It was not until the 1990s, with artists like Juan Luis Guerra , that Bachata gained international recognition. 2000s The pop evolution In the early 2000s, the group Aventura revolutionized the genre by infusing it with R&B and Pop elements. Deep Dive into the Roots Want to know why Bachata was prohibited and how it became a global sensation? Start with our complete guide to Bachata music and dance . Read the full story Bachata Styles Explained As Bachata spread across the globe, it evolved into distinct styles. Understanding these differences helps you respect the roots while enjoying modern interpretations. Mastering each style is essential to becoming a complete dancer, as different songs and energies call for different ways of moving. Dominican (Traditional) The Roots. This is the original style danced in the DR. It focuses heavily on footwork (steps) rather than turns. Music Faster tempo, guitar-dominated, raw acoustic sound. Movement Focus on footwork (steps), playful syncopations, and hip movement. Connection Typically open or close position, focusing on rhythmic partnership. Bachata Fusion The Fusion. A bridge between the two. It incorporates the turn patterns of Salsa and the basic steps of Traditional. Music Urban fusion, incorporating R&B, Pop, and Hip-Hop elements. Movement Turn patterns, cross-body leads, and intricate arm work. Connection Dynamic interplay, frequently switching between open and closed holds. Bachata Sensual The Evolution. Created in Cádiz, Spain, by Korke & Judith. It interprets the music through body isolations and waves. Music Modern, melodic remixes or pop, with less heavy guitar. Movement Flowy body isolations, waves, and circular movements. Connection Close contact position, leading through frame and body points. Curious? Read our Bachata Sensual guide or start with the Foundation course . Terms covered — now learn the manners: our dance etiquette guide . Musicality Guide Bachata music is driven by a specific set of instruments. Learning to listen to them allows you to predict the music and dance "in the pocket." Requinto (Lead Guitar) The melodic leader. It plays the intro, the solos, and sets the mood. Dancers often follow the Requinto with their footwork. Segunda (Rhythm Guitar) Adds syncopation and harmony. It supports the Requinto and fills the rhythmic space. Bass (Bajo) The heartbeat. It usually plays on beats 1, 3, and 4 (often holding the 4). It drives the energy and signals section changes. Bongo The rhythmic engine. The heavy hit on the 4th beat (the "Macho" drum) is what gives Bachata its drive. Güira The metal scraper. It keeps the timing and adds the high-frequency texture that makes the music danceable. Simplified eight-count phrase. Counts 4 and 8 are the tap — the accent that gives Bachata its drive. Song Structure Bachata songs are typically divided into four main sections: Intro , Derecho (Verse - steady beat), Majao (Chorus - upbeat rhythm with bongo rolls), and Mambo (High energy, instrumental section). Good dancers anticipate these changes to adjust their energy and movement style accordingly. Go deeper: Finding the “One” in Bachata music . Dance Glossary Basic Step Three steps to the side followed by a tap (or hip movement) on the 4th beat. Tap Touching the floor with the toe without transferring weight. Marks the end of a 4-count phrase. Isolation Moving one part of the body (e.g., chest, hips) while keeping the rest still. Key for Sensual style. Frame The structure of the arms and upper body that allows the lead and follow to communicate connection. Prep A preparatory movement for a step or body movement. Social A party or event focused on social dancing rather than classes or performances. Musicality The ability to interpret the music through dance, matching movement to rhythm and melody. # Page: Dance Etiquette | AXcent Dance Zurich (etiquette.html)
Description: Learn the essential rules of social dancing. A guide to dance floor etiquette, hygiene, and respect for the Bachata community.

Dance Etiquette | AXcent Dance Zurich AXcent DANCE Home About us Our classes Prices & Registration Events Contact Login More ▾ Room Rental Corporate Events Wedding Dance Private Lessons Gallery Education Beginner Guide Blog FAQ Dance Etiquette Contact Book Free Trial EN | DE COMMUNITY GUIDELINES Dance Floor Etiquette Respect, hygiene, and kindness make the dance floor a better place for everyone. If you are starting fresh, our beginner Bachata guide can also help. The Golden Rules 01 Asking for a Dance Anyone can ask! Be polite, make eye contact, and extend your hand. Accept a "No" gracefully. 02 Hygiene Matters Fresh breath and deodorant are musts. Bring a spare shirt if needed. Your partner will thank you! 03 Saying Thank You Always thank your partner at the end of the dance. It shows appreciation for the shared moment. 04 Respect Boundaries If a partner prefers a open hold or more distance, respect it immediately without question. 05 Be Gentle Lead and follow with care. Never force a move or grip too tightly. Safety comes first. On the Dance Floor 01 Floorcraft Watch out for others. Avoid big moves on a crowded floor and protect your partner from collisions. 02 No Teaching Unless asked, do not teach on the social floor. Focus on connecting and having fun, not perfection. 03 Smile & Connect Connection beats complexity. Relax, listen to the music, and enjoy the dance. A smile goes a long way! 04 No Aerials Lifts and aerials are for shows, not the social floor. Keep your feet on the ground for safety. 05 Small Steps When the floor is packed, keep your steps small and under your body to save space. Class Rules 01 No Chewing Gum For safety reasons, please dispose of chewing gum before class starts. 02 Let the Teacher Teach Please do not correct other students. If you see an issue, focus on your own dancing. 03 Stay Active If you are tired, take a break outside the line. Sitting in class lowers the energy of the group. 04 Ask Questions Properly Do not step into the middle to ask. Please raise your hand and wait for the teacher. 05 Be Punctual Arrive on time to warm up properly and not miss important initial instructions. First social night coming up? Read the beginner guide — or come practice with us first. # Page: What is Bachata Sensual? | AXcent Dance Zurich (guide-bachata-sensual.html)
Description: Learn about Bachata Sensual, a modern fusion style focusing on body movement and connection. The main style taught at AXcent Dance Zurich.

What is Bachata Sensual? | AXcent Dance Zurich AXcent DANCE Home About us Our classes Prices & Registration Events Contact Login More ▾ Room Rental Corporate Events Wedding Dance Private Lessons Gallery Education Beginner Guide Blog FAQ Dance Etiquette Contact Book Free Trial EN | DE OUR SPECIALTY What is Bachata Sensual? A modern evolution of the dance that has taken Europe by storm. It's about flow, feeling, and expressing the music with your whole body. Bachata Sensual was created in Spain by Korke & Judith. It respects the traditional basic steps of Bachata but adds more complex body movements, isolations, and circular figures. If you want to understand the roots first, read our guide to Bachata music and dance . While traditional Bachata focuses more on footwork and playful partner interaction, Bachata Sensual focuses more on the connection between the partners and interpreting the melody and emotion of the song. Key Elements Body Waves: Smooth, flowing movements of the body. Isolations: Moving one part of the body (like the chest or hips) while keeping the rest still. Close Connection: A comfortable, respectful embrace that allows for subtle leading and following. Is it too intimate? The name "Sensual" can sometimes be misleading. It refers to "sensing" the music and the partner's movement, not necessarily sexual intimacy. At AXcent Dance, we place a huge emphasis on respect and boundaries . We teach you how to lead and follow these movements safely and comfortably, ensuring that both partners feel good. It is about creating a beautiful dance together, not about being inappropriate. Why learn with us? Our instructors are certified and trained in the official Bachata Sensual methodology. We focus on proper technique so you can execute these movements safely and look great doing it. Ready to learn it? Bachata Sensual Foundation , Wednesdays 19:30, is the entry course into the style — see the full course page . # Page: What is Bachata? Music and Dance Guide | AXcent Zurich (guide-bachata.html)
Description: What is Bachata? Learn the music, instruments, rhythm, dance styles, and Dominican roots in this complete guide for Bachata dancers in Zurich.

What is Bachata? Music and Dance Guide | AXcent Zurich AXcent DANCE Home About us Our classes Prices & Registration Events Contact Login More ▾ Room Rental Corporate Events Wedding Dance Private Lessons Gallery Education Beginner Guide Blog FAQ Dance Etiquette Contact Book Free Trial EN | DE What is Bachata? What is Bachata? Inside the Bachata Sound What is Bachata? It is a conversation between metal, wood, skin, strings, and voice. Follow the five instruments that create the feeling behind every step. Güira Bongos Segunda Bass Requinto Section 01 The Bachata Rhythmic Pulse The güira is the bright metal pulse that keeps Bachata moving. Its rasp cuts through the band with a steady stream of texture, marking time while adding the crisp snap that makes the rhythm feel alive. For dancers, it is one of the easiest sounds to follow when finding the groove. Listen for the scratch, the release, and the tiny accents between the main beats; they create the shimmering energy that makes Bachata feel playful instead of flat. Section 02 El Martillo The bongos speak in two voices: the smaller macho drum gives sharper tones, while the larger hembra drum brings a rounder, deeper answer. Together they play el martillo, the hammer pattern that gives Bachata its unmistakable bounce. This rhythm does more than keep time. It converses with the güira, opens space for breaks, and often signals changes in energy. When the bongos improvise, dancers feel it as a lift, a pause, or a sudden invitation to play with the music. Section 03 Chop And Harmony The segunda, also called the rítmica, is the rhythm guitar that gives Bachata its forward push. Instead of taking the spotlight, it locks into short chord chops, muted strums, and syncopated accents that glue the percussion and harmony together. Its job is subtle but essential. The segunda shapes the feel of the song: relaxed and romantic in softer passages, sharper and more percussive when the music drives. Without it, Bachata loses much of the spring that dancers feel under their steps. Section 04 The Bachata Bass Foundation The bass is the floor of the whole arrangement. It anchors the harmony, outlines the chord changes, and often walks with a melodic quality that feels almost like a second singer underneath the guitars. In Bachata, the bass does not simply sit on the beat. It pushes, answers, and creates counterpoint against the bongos and guitars. For dancers, it gives weight to the body and helps make the tap, pause, or hip action feel grounded rather than decorative. Section 05 The Singing Requinto The requinto is the lead guitar, the voice that most people recognize first in Bachata. It plays bright arpeggios, melodic hooks, fills, and solos that give the song its emotional signature. It can sound sweet, nostalgic, playful, or dramatic within just a few notes. When the requinto answers the singer or rises above the band, it tells dancers where the feeling is: when to soften, when to accent, and when to let the music breathe. From Sound To Social Dance Bachata began in the Dominican Republic and grew from intimate guitar music into one of the most loved social dances in the world. The basic dance structure is approachable: three steps and a tap, danced to a warm 4/4 rhythm with space for play, connection, and musicality. For a wider learning path, explore our Bachata education hub . The magic is that the music feels simple at first and then keeps revealing detail. The güira gives shimmer, the bongos speak in syncopation, the segunda drives the groove, the bass walks, and the requinto sings over everything. Styles You Will Meet Dominican Bachata: footwork, musicality, playful partner conversation. Bachata Moderna: turns and figures influenced by salsa and modern partner dance. Bachata Sensual: body movement, connection, and expressive flow. Ready to hear it in your own steps? Join a structured Bachata class in Zurich Altstetten and connect the rhythm, instruments, partnerwork, and dance floor from the first lesson. # Page: What is Social Dancing? | AXcent Dance Zurich (guide-social-dancing.html)
Description: Learn about social dancing, a fun and inclusive way to meet people and express yourself. Perfect for beginners in Zurich.

What is Social Dancing? | AXcent Dance Zurich AXcent DANCE Home About us Our classes Prices & Registration Events Contact Login More ▾ Room Rental Corporate Events Wedding Dance Private Lessons Gallery Education Beginner Guide Blog FAQ Dance Etiquette Contact Book Free Trial EN | DE NEWCOMER GUIDE What is Social Dancing? Forget everything you know about choreographed routines. Social dancing is about improvisation, connection, and having fun in the moment. 01 What is Social Dancing? If you have ever watched "Dancing with the Stars" and thought, "I could never remember all those steps," we have good news for you: Social dancing is completely different. Social dancing is not about performing for an audience. It is about dancing with a partner for the sheer enjoyment of it. It happens at parties, clubs, and socials, where people of all ages and backgrounds come together to share a passion for music and movement. 02 The Magic of Leading & Following In social dancing, there is no set choreography. Instead, we use a language of physical signals called "leading and following." One person (the leader) suggests a movement, and the other (the follower) interprets it. This creates a unique, improvised dance every single time. 03 Do I need a partner? Absolutely not! This is the biggest myth about social dancing. In fact, most people come to classes alone. In our courses, we rotate partners frequently. This helps you learn faster because you get used to leading or following different people, not just one specific person. It is also a fantastic way to make new friends. The social dance community in Zurich is incredibly welcoming and diverse. 04 Is it hard to learn? Like any new skill, it takes a little practice, but the basics are easier than you think. Our Beginner 2 courses are perfect if you have approx. 4-8 months of experience. Our beginner Bachata guide is a helpful starting point if you are newer to dance. We build the technique step by step, with a focus on flow, footwork, and movement quality. (Absolute beginners without any experience should check our upcoming schedule for new course start dates). Ready to give it a try? Join us for a trial class or sign up for the full course. REGISTER NOW Know the floor rules before your first social night — read our dance etiquette guide , then come practice at our events and socials . # Page: Bachata Beginner 1 Kurs Zürich | Grundlagen Lernen (de/bachata-beginner-1.html)
Description: Lerne die Bachata Grundlagen in Zürich. Unser Beginner 1 Kurs für Einsteiger deckt einfache Drehungen, Media und Basis-Partnerwork ab. Ohne Partner!

Bachata Beginner 1 Kurs Zürich | Grundlagen Lernen AXcent DANCE Home Über uns Unsere Kurse Preise & Anmeldung Events Kontakt Login Mehr ▾ Raumvermietung Firmenevents Hochzeitstanz Privatstunden Galerie Ausbildung Anfänger Guide Blog FAQ Tanzetikette Kontakt Probelektion buchen EN | DE Wöchentlicher Kurs · Montags 19:30 Bachata Beginner 1 Der Einstieg in deine Bachata-Reise — der 8-Schritte-Basic, deine ersten Drehungen und entspanntes Partnerwork, Schritt für Schritt unterrichtet und ganz ohne Vorwissen. Neu beim Tanzen? Unser Anfänger Guide ist die richtige erste Lektüre. Tag & Zeit Montags, 19:30 Niveau ~2–4 Monate Tanzerfahrung oder frisch aus Beginner 0 Studio Hermetschloostrasse 73, Zurich Altstetten Sprache Englisch Block 8 Wochen · 220 CHF (Studierende 185 CHF) Einstieg 8-Wochen-Blöcke · die erste Klasse ist kostenlos Kostenlose Probelektion buchen Für den Kurs anmelden Komm, wie du bist — das Versprechen von Beginner 1. Was du lernen wirst Fünf Bausteine, Woche für Woche aufgebaut — die Grundlagen des Tanzens , auf denen jedes höhere Level aufbaut. 01 Der 8-Schritte-Basic Der fundamentale Bachata-Grundschritt in alle Richtungen — der Schritt, auf dem jeder Tanz aufbaut, den du je tanzen wirst. 02 Einfache Drehungen Deine ersten Turn Patterns für Leader und Follower, unterrichtet mit der richtigen Verbindung, damit sie sich leicht statt gehetzt anfühlen. 03 Die klassische “Media” Die halbe Drehung, die Übergänge geschmeidig macht — eine Bachata-Signatur, die du ab der ersten Woche brauchst. 04 Einfaches Partnerwork Wie du bequem hältst, führst und folgst, damit sich das Tanzen zu zweit vom ersten Lied an natürlich anfühlt. 05 Timing, Rhythmus & Isolation Wo der Beat in der Musik lebt und wie du deinen Körper mit ihm bewegen lässt — eine Einführung in die Bachata-Musikalität. Alles hier kehrt in jedem höheren Level zurück — deshalb unterrichten wir es langsam, gründlich und ganz ohne Vorwissen. Ist das dein Kurs? “Ich habe ein paar Wochen oder Monate Grundlagen — ich will sie richtig aufbauen.” Du bist hier genau richtig. Beginner 1 setzt höchstens eine einfache Drehung, die Media und entspanntes Basis-Partnerwork voraus — und wir wiederholen alles davon unterwegs. “Ich habe in meinem Leben noch keinen Tanzschritt gemacht.” Du bist trotzdem willkommen — jeder Schritt wird von null unterrichtet. Wenn du lieber in einem Raum voller Erstanfänger startest, beginne mit Bachata Beginner 0 , montags 18:30. Lies den Anfänger Guide . Nicht sicher? Buche eine kostenlose Probelektion — wir teilen dich ein. So läuft eine Klasse ab Sechzig Minuten, ein Schritt, viele Partner. 01 Aufwärmen & Wiederholung Schüttle den Tag ab, komm an und wiederhole die Schritte der letzten Woche. 02 Der Schritt der Woche Ein neuer Baustein, langsam aufgeschlüsselt — zuerst die Füsse, dann das Timing. 03 Hinein ins Partnerwork Derselbe Schritt zu zweit getanzt, in einem Tempo, bei dem niemand zurückbleibt. 04 Rotieren & tanzen Die Partner rotieren während der Klasse — am Ende hast du mit allen getanzt. Lerne deine Lehrer kennen Ale & Xidan Gründer, internationale Bachata-Künstler und offizielle Wertungsrichter der IDO Swiss Championship — sie unterrichten diesen Kurs persönlich. Mehr über uns Wohin dieser Kurs führt Beginner 1 Montags 19:30 · du bist hier Beginner 2 Dienstags 19:30 Sensual Foundation Mittwochs 19:30 Sensual Improver Mittwochs 20:30 Mittelstufe / Fortgeschritten Donnerstags 19:30 & 20:30 Die erste Klasse ist kostenlos Komm einmal vorbei, tanze die ganze Stunde und entscheide danach. Falls Beginner 1 nicht der richtige Kurs für dich ist, teilen wir dich in das passende Level ein. Kostenlose Probelektion buchen Für den Kurs anmelden 8-Wochen-Block · 220 CHF (27.50 pro Klasse) · 15% Rabatt auf deine erste Anmeldung · Studierendenrabatt · Kein Abo Eine echte Person bestätigt deinen Platz per WhatsApp. Gute Fragen Brauche ich Vorkenntnisse? Nein. Eine einfache Drehung, die Media und einfaches Partnerwork helfen — und alles davon wird Schritt für Schritt unterrichtet, wenn du ohne sie ankommst. Absolute Erstanfänger können auch mit Bachata Beginner 0 montags um 19:30 starten. Kann ich mitten in einem Block einsteigen? Frag uns, bevor du mitten im Block einsteigst — wir sagen dir ehrlich, ob die aktuelle Woche ein guter Einstiegspunkt ist. Die Probelektion ist so oder so kostenlos. Brauche ich einen Partner? Nein. Die Partner rotieren während der Klasse, sodass du mit allen tanzt — die meisten kommen alleine. Was soll ich anziehen? Bequeme Kleidung, in der du dich frei bewegen kannst, und Schuhe, mit denen du dich drehen kannst — saubere Sneakers sind ideal. Kommst du direkt von der Arbeit? Ein frisches Shirt, Deo und Mints machen die Stunde für alle angenehmer. Unser Guide zur passenden Kleidung hat alle Details. Was, wenn ich eine Woche verpasse? Bist du krank, kannst du eine verpasste Klasse pro Semester in einem anderen passenden Kurs nachholen. Die vollständige Richtlinie findest du in unseren AGB .
